samples.summary: `quietDeadline` is anchored before the `fonts.ready` race, so the 3s "quiet" budget is not a 3s wait — it is whatever (often zero) is left after `fonts.ready` consumed up to the full 10s
samples.evidence: `const quietDeadline = start + Math.min(timeoutMs, quietMs)` (line 410) is measured from `start`, but the code then does `await Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, sleep(deadline - now)])` (lines 477-480) *before* the poll loop that uses `quietDeadline` (line 490: `const quiet = loading.length === 0 || now >= quietDeadline`). Two consequences, both contradicting the stated design: (a) if a non-floor face (KaTeX / eager catalog) stalls, `fonts.ready` stays pending and the race burns the full FONT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS, so the stall costs 10s per pass, not the "seconds, not the full timeout" the comment at lines 381-385 claims; (b) once >3s has elapsed in that race, `now >= quietDeadline` is already true on the very first poll iteration, so the soft wait for a late-injected link's in-flight fetch never actually waits at all — the check is effectively dead. The success-path warning at lines 537-540 then reports `still fetching after ${FONT_QUIET_TIMEOUT_MS}ms` even though the real wait was 0ms or 10000ms. Fix would be to anchor `quietDeadline` at the moment the poll loop begins.

samples.summary: New refetch mechanism (remove + re-insert the same `<link>` with an unchanged href) may not trigger any refetch in Blink, so the only recovery path for an `error` face becomes a no-op that still costs two extra 10s settle passes
samples.evidence: `refetchPass` (lines 505-517) now does `link.remove(); parent.insertBefore(link, next);` and deliberately drops the previous `wbVisualRetry` cache-buster (comment lines 499-504). A re-inserted link with an unchanged href is served from Chromium's memory/HTTP cache, and Blink may reuse the link element's already-parsed CSSStyleSheet, in which case the same FontFace objects — including any stuck in `status: "error"` — are re-registered rather than recreated and no woff2 fetch is retried. That is exactly the case the retry loop exists for (see comment lines 361-364: "A face whose woff2 fetch failed sits in `status: \"error\"` for good ... only a refetch can"). If the re-insert does not force a fresh fetch, FONT_REFETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 buys nothing but ~20s of extra waiting per failing pass before the same failure is recorded. Nothing in the tree verifies the re-insert actually refetches (no test, no assertion on request counts).

samples.summary: The new `refetched === 0` early-exit records a failure but never sets `webFontRefetchExhausted`, so the "stop burning time once the network is broken" guard does not cover this permanent, unrecoverable condition
samples.evidence: Lines 553-561: when there is no fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet at all (a permanent condition — index.html's link is gone for every pass), the failure is pushed and the function returns without setting `webFontRefetchExhausted = true`, unlike the sibling exhaustion branch at line 545. Every one of the remaining ~24 passes therefore repeats the full FONT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS settle plus a pointless `refetchPass` evaluate and duplicate error log, for an outcome that is already known to be unrecoverable — the exact cost the flag was introduced to avoid (comment lines 391-394).

samples.summary: The `requested` dedupe set was removed, so `loadRequired()` re-issues all 9 `document.fonts.load()` calls on every 100ms poll tick
samples.evidence: The previous implementation kept a `requested` Set keyed `${weight} ${family}` and skipped already-requested pairs; the new `loadRequired()` (lines 422-435) has no dedupe and is called again at line 494 on each tick. Over a 10s settle that is up to ~100 × 9 = ~900 `fonts.load()` invocations, each creating a promise (and a rejected-then-swallowed promise for faces in `status: "error"`). Functionally tolerable because `fonts.load()` coalesces in-flight loads, but it is unnecessary churn inside a tight poll and a behavioral regression versus the code it replaced.

samples.summary: The comment justifying the narrowed gate asserts eager catalog families are not painted by screenshots, but `ThemedFontPicker`'s SYSTEM list renders a row in `Roboto` (an `eager: true` catalog web font) and `slides-pickers` screenshots it
samples.evidence: Comment lines 342-352 claim "`FONT_CATALOG`'s eager Korean/Roboto set is likewise registered on slides/docs mounts without every screenshot painting it". But `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/themed-font-picker-helpers.ts:12-21` lists `Roboto`, `themed-font-picker.tsx:117` renders each SYSTEM row `style={{ fontFamily: family }}`, and `font-catalog.data.ts:49` marks Roboto `eager: true`. So in any pass where the eager Google Fonts link is present (`useGoogleFontsLink()` in slides-view.tsx:230 / docs-view.tsx:210), the `slides-pickers` target paints a web-font family that is outside REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS and therefore no longer gated — the same drift class the change is meant to close. Currently mitigated only by the harness rendering the picker standalone (no `useGoogleFontsLink`), which makes the gate correct by accident rather than by design and silently regresses if a scenario ever mounts the real view.

samples.summary: No gate (not even the soft one) covers a lazily injected font link whose faces are still `unloaded`: `stillLoading()` only sees `status: "loading"`, so "registered but fetch not started" counts as quiet and the capture proceeds
samples.evidence: `stillLoading()` (lines 466-472) collects only faces with `status === "loading"`. A link injected by a mount effect registers its @font-face rules with status `unloaded` until text using them is laid out and Chromium starts the fetch; between registration and fetch start the registry is "quiet", `missingRequired()` ignores the family (it is outside REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS), and the screenshot is taken against fallback glyphs. The delta's own comment (lines 348-351) claims this soft check "is what actually catches a late-injected per-family link (ThemedFontPicker)" — it only catches it in the narrow window where the fetch has already begun.
searchedFor: grep for ensureFontLink / useGoogleFontsLink call sites

verdict.reason: The code exists as described (refetchPass at verify-visual-browser.mjs:505-517 re-inserts the same <link> with an unchanged href, cache-buster deliberately dropped per the comment at 499-504 and the history note in docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:103-106), but it is not a blocking correctness defect. (a) Outcome correctness is unaffected either way: if the re-insert refetches nothing, the loop still exits at 544-550, records the pass in webFontFailures, prints the missing families by name, exits non-zero at 821-823, and refuses to record baselines at 707-712 — no silent pass, no crash, no data loss, no baseline overwrite. (b) The finding's stated cost is factually wrong: webFontRefetchExhausted (declared :395, read :524, set :545) forces maxAttempts=0 for all later passes, so the extra ~20s is paid once per run, not "per failing pass"; the loop terminates cleanly with no hang. (c) The central assertion is unverified speculation about Blink's stylesheet/FontFace reuse, with no repro, test, or request-count evidence anywhere in the tree. Worst case is a weaker transient-failure recovery heuristic in a dev-only screenshot harness that still fails loudly and accurately — minor/nit impact under the Correctness rubric, not critical/major.

finding.summary: An empty/partial font registry is reported as "settled", so a blocked or failed Google Fonts stylesheet passes silently with fallback glyphs
finding.evidence: `pending(families)` only iterates families that are *already registered* in `document.fonts`. If the `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...` stylesheet in `index.html` (or a lazily injected per-family link) never loads — DNS blocked, 4xx, offline runner — Chromium registers no @font-face rules at all for it, so `registry()` returns an empty (or Inter-less) Map, `pending()` returns `[]`, and `waitForFontsReady` returns success on attempt 0. The capture then paints the browser default serif, which is exactly the drift this PR exists to detect. Grep shows the frontend declares no local `@font-face` anywhere (only comments mention it), so with the CDN unreachable `document.fonts` is genuinely empty and the guard degenerates to a no-op. The same holds for `if (!document.fonts) return []` (line 377). Worse, in `UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE=true` mode the new "Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs" guard (line 640) never fires, so fallback-glyph baselines get committed. Needs an assertion that the expected Google Fonts links resolved / that at least the known-eager families are present, not just "nothing registered is missing".

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. There is no `pending()`/`registry()` pair and no `if (!document.fonts) return []`; line 377 is a `REQUIRED_WEB_FONTS` entry. The floor is asserted positively over a hard-coded family list (verify-visual-browser.mjs:374-378, :439) that mirrors the css2 query in packages/frontend/index.html:12, and the exact "unreachable stylesheet registers nothing" case is the first failure branch: `if (faces.length === 0) missing.push(`${family} (no @font-face registered)`)` (:444-447), with `document.fonts` unavailable also returning a non-empty `missing` (:405-407). A non-empty `missing` bypasses the success return at :528-542, triggers refetch (:552) and records `webFontFailures` (:546, :556), which makes the baseline guard at :707-712 exit(1) rather than never fire. So an empty/partial registry is reported as a failure, not as "settled".

finding.summary: Cache-busting param appended to the css2 URL may make Google Fonts return an error payload, dropping every @font-face and (with the finding above) turning failure into a silent pass
finding.evidence: `url.searchParams.set("wbVisualRetry", String(attempt))` rewrites the app's own `<link>` href in place. The comment asserts "css2 ignores it" with no verification; the css2 endpoint is documented as strict about its query grammar and can answer an invalid request with an error CSS body / non-200. If that happens, the refetch removes every previously-registered face from `document.fonts` (the old sheet is dropped when href changes), so the next settle sees an empty registry and returns `[]` — reported as success — and the app's link stays permanently pointed at the broken URL for the rest of that page's life. The recovery path can therefore convert a detected failure into an undetected one.

verdict.reason: The claimed code does not exist in this repository. `refetchPass` at packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs:505-517 recovers by removing and re-inserting the same `<link rel='stylesheet']` element (`link.remove(); parent.insertBefore(link, next);`) — the `href` is never mutated and no query parameter is added. A repo-wide grep for `wbVisualRetry` matches only docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:103 (a retrospective describing the superseded approach) and .agent-review artifacts; there is no occurrence in any source file. A grep for `searchParams|cache-bust|cacheBust` across packages/frontend/scripts returns a single hit — the comment at line 501 stating that no cache-busting param is appended, precisely so a working css2 request cannot be turned into a rejected one. The finding's chained premise also fails independently: the settle pass asserts registration positively at lines 444-447 (`if (faces.length === 0) missing.push(`${family} (no @font-face registered)`)`), so an emptied `document.fonts` registry yields a non-empty `missing` list, which is reported as a failure at lines 544-550 and exits non-zero at lines 694-705 / 821-823 rather than being reported as success. The described "detected failure converted into an undetected one" path therefore has no mechanism in this code.
